name: Jahana Hayes
page_title: Jahana Hayes' Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic for U.S. House (CT) - District 5

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "The Supreme Court decision to overturn Roe v. Wade reverses fifty years of precedent and goes against the spirit of the Constitution. It is the right of every person to exercise autonomy over their body. I have consistently fought against legislation attempting to limit access to abortion and other contraceptive care, and voted to pass legislation which would codify the right to choose into law. Connecticut leads the nation in policy to protect access to contraceptive care, and I will continue to fight so these rights are not undermined at the federal level. I support proposals that expand access to contraception and sex education so every person’s reproductive choices remain between them and their doctor."
Rated 100% by Planned Parenthood Action Fund
Voted in favor of HR 8296: "Women's Health Protection Act of 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 8297: "Ensuring Access to Abortion Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: "Health care costs, prescription drug costs, and insurance premiums continue to skyrocket. These unjustifiable costs are not victimless – they are causing Americans to die. 34 million Americans report that they have a friend or family member who has died because they could not afford health care. I will always support legislation that expands access to affordable health care for more people. I have worked to ensure that healthcare is affordable, accessible, and equitable. Most recently, I voted to lower health insurance premiums under the Affordable Care Act."
"Health care is a right, not a privilege. I am committed to making sure everyone has access to healthcare."

"I am a cosponsor of Medicare for All as the proposal that will provide the most affordable, equitable health care to all Americans. Additionally, I have supported proposals that make incremental improvements toward that goal."
Voted in favor of HR 1425: "Patient Protection and Affordable Care Enhancement Act"

positions.question: Do you support expanding paid family AND/OR medical leave benefits (e.g. maternity leave)?

evidence.text: "At some point, every worker will need to take time away from a job to care for their health, a child or a family member–but millions still lack access to paid family and medical leave. Call your Senators and urge them to pass the #HEROES Act."

"The U.S. is the only industrialized country in the world w/ NO national paid family leave policy. We must go beyond #FMLA and make #PaidLeaveForAll a reality so everyone can take the time they deserve to heal and be there for their loved ones w/o sacrificing financial security."

"When women succeed, we all succeed – our families, the workforce, & the economy. I joined the @Labor_Caucus for a discussion with @AFLCIO on the importance of supporting women in the workplace through meaningful investments in paid leave, pay equity, & affordable childcare."
Voted in favor of HR 6201 "Families First Coronavirus Response Act"

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "History has been made! @POTUS has signed the Inflation Reduction Act into law - lowering health care costs, cutting prescription drug prices, and improving energy costs for American families."

"Since entering Congress, I have forcefully advocated to lower prescription costs for all Americans. I voted for legislation which banned the practice of surprise billing and supported legislation to cap insulin costs for all Americans at $35. Most recently, I voted for the Inflation Reduction Act, historic legislation which allows Medicare to negotiate drug prices directly with pharmaceutical companies, caps annual Medicare Part D out of pocket costs at $2,000, and caps Medicare covered insulin costs at $35 a month. The bill also penalizes manufacturers who raise prescription drug prices faster than the rate of inflation. These changes will dramatically lower the cost of prescription drugs for millions of Medicare recipients."
Voted in favor of HR 3 "Lower Drug Costs Now Act of 2019"
Voted in favor of HR 6833 "The Affordable Insulin Now Act"
